questions.question: Compare spiral and elliptical galaxies using observable properties such as star / population, gas content, and structure.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare spiral and elliptical galaxies using observable properties such as star population, gas
  • content, and structure.
  • Elliptical galaxies are egg shaped. They range from nearly perfect spheres, E0, to the flattest, E7.
  • Elliptical galaxies seem to contain practically all old stars. They have little visible gas and dust
  • but infrared and X-ray observations reveal some. - (2 marks)
  • Spiral galaxies have a disk with central bulge and spiral arms. They are divided into two
  • subcategories. Normal spiral galaxies with a bright disk where spiral arms wind out from a
  • bulging nucleus. For the Barred spiral galaxies the spiral arms unwind from the ends of a
  • bar-shaped concentration of material. Spiral galaxies have large amounts of gas and dust in the
  • disk and contain young, middle-aged, and old stars. - (3 marks)
questions.final_answer: disk and contain young, middle-aged, and old stars
